<!-- Generated by `make docs-sync` (tools/gendocs/modules) from the module's Doc method. Do not edit by hand. -->

Manages a single iptables (or ip6tables) rule, identified by its full spec (chain + match args + target) rather than a name. Idempotent: a rule is only appended/inserted or deleted when its presence differs from the declared state.

**Category:** Firewall (base)

## States

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `present` | The rule exists in the chain (`iptables -C` succeeds); Apply appends it (`-A`) or inserts it at `position` (`-I`) if missing. Existing rules are never reordered. |
| `absent` | The rule does not exist in the chain; Apply runs `-D` until every matching copy is removed. |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chain` | string | yes | Target chain, built-in or custom, e.g. `INPUT`, `POSTROUTING`. |
| `rule` | string | yes | The match spec + target only, e.g. `-p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT`. May also be given as a list of args. Must not include `-t`, `-A/-I/-D/-C/-R`, `-N`, or `-P` — the module supplies the table and action. |
| `table` | string |  | One of `filter`, `nat`, `mangle`, `raw`, `security`. Default: `filter`. |
| `family` | string |  | Address family: `ipv4` (iptables) or `ipv6` (ip6tables). Default: `ipv4`. |
| `position` | int |  | Insert position for `-I` (1-based); `0` (default) appends with `-A`. Allowed on `present` only. |
| `save` | string |  | Absolute path to write `iptables-save` output to after a change. |

## Examples

### Allow inbound SSH

```yaml
iptables:
  allow-ssh:
    state: present
    chain: INPUT
    rule: "-p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT"
```

### Insert an IPv6 NAT rule and persist the ruleset

`position: 1` inserts at the head of the chain; `save` writes ip6tables-save output.

```yaml
iptables:
  masquerade-v6:
    state: present
    chain: POSTROUTING
    table: nat
    family: ipv6
    rule:
      - -o
      - eth0
      - -j
      - MASQUERADE
    position: 1
    save: /etc/iptables/rules.v6
```

### Remove a blocked source

```yaml
iptables:
  drop-bad-host:
    state: absent
    chain: INPUT
    rule: "-s 10.0.0.5 -j DROP"
    save: /etc/iptables/rules.v4
```

## Notes

- Linux only — the rule is checked/applied via the iptables/ip6tables binaries; other operating systems return an unsupported-OS error.
- A rule has no name: its identity is the full spec, so the declaration name is just a human label. The module never moves an existing rule (no order management).
- Out of scope (v0.x candidates, #114): a structured rule model (proto/dport/jump à la Salt), ordering guarantees, `family: both` in one declaration, distro persistence integration (netfilter-persistent / the iptables service) beyond a plain `save:`, iptables-nft vs iptables-legacy selection, and chain creation/policy. nftables is its own module.
